record.paper_title: Some problems and conjectures about L2-invariants
record.original_question: If M is an aspherical closed topological manifold of odd dimension 2m+1, must M be det-L2-acyclic with L2-torsion satisfying (-1)^m ρ^{(2)}(M̃) ≥ 0? If M is a closed smooth (2m+1)-manifold with a negatively curved Riemannian metric, must one have the strict inequality (-1)^m ρ^{(2)}(M̃) > 0? And if M is aspherical of odd dimension and π_1(M) contains an amenable infinite normal subgroup, must ρ^{(2)}(M̃) vanish?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.3 (Hopf Conjecture for L2-torsion). If M is an aspherical closed topological manifold of odd dimension dim(M) = 2m+ 1, then M is det-L2-acyclic, and its L2-torsion satisfies (−1)m · ρ(2)(Mf) ≥ 0. If M is a closed smooth manifold of odd dimension dim(M) = 2m + 1 with Riemannian metric and with sectional curvature sec(M) < 0, then M is det-L2-acyclic, and its L2-torsion satisfies (−1)m · ρ(2)(Mf) > 0. If M is an aspherical closed topological manifold of odd dimension dim(M) = 2m+1 whose fundamental group contains an amenable infinite normal subgroup, then M is det-L2-acyclic and its L2-torsion satisfies ρ(2)(Mf) = 0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let M be a closed aspherical topological manifold of odd dimension 2m+1, and let M̃ denote its universal cover. Recall that M̃ is called det-L²-acyclic if its reduced L²-homology vanishes and the Fuglede–Kadison determinants of the combinatorial Laplacians on M̃ (with respect to the action of π₁(M) on cellular L²-chains) are well defined and equal to 1 in the appropriate sense, so that the L²-torsion ρ^{(2)}(M̃) ∈ ℝ is defined.

Prove or disprove the following three assertions:

(a) Every closed aspherical topological manifold M of odd dimension 2m+1 is det-L²-acyclic, and its L²-torsion satisfies
   (−1)^m · ρ^{(2)}(M̃) ≥ 0.

(b) If, in addition, M admits a smooth structure and a Riemannian metric of strictly negative sectional curvature, then M is det-L²-acyclic and
   (−1)^m · ρ^{(2)}(M̃) > 0.

(c) If M is a closed aspherical topological manifold of odd dimension 2m+1 whose fundamental group π₁(M) contains an infinite amenable normal subgroup, then M is det-L²-acyclic and
   ρ^{(2)}(M̃) = 0.
artifact.status_search_result: The three-part statement is a well-known conjecture (Hopf-type conjecture for L²-torsion) due to Lück. Recent surveys by Lück and related works (2024–2025) continue to list it among the open problems on aspherical manifolds and L²-invariants; no proof or counterexample is known in general, although special cases (e.g., locally symmetric spaces of noncompact type, certain 3-manifolds) are verified.

status_evidence.title: A Survey on L2-torsion (W. Lück)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing the Hopf-type conjecture for L²-torsion in odd dimensions as a still open conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture remains open in general.

status_evidence.title: Some open problems about aspherical closed manifolds (W. Lück)
status_evidence.snippet: Lists L²-torsion sign conjectures for aspherical odd-dimensional manifolds among open problems.
